Lock OFF (default): ro_begin_abort +4.5%, rw_empty_commit +9.4% (both regressed, all 5 rounds), commit/batch/n1 +2.1% flat, get/* flat. hypothesis: ADR-0023 stage 1 fix: resolving the reader-slot storage once per operation (fixed-layout ReaderSlot slice, no per-slot enum match or virtual call) and moving the lock-file arms of write_txn out of line removes the default-path regression and cuts the lock-file cost.
notes: Branch-only (not merged). CGU1, 5 rounds, bench server, three-sided driver; rungs above = lock ON vs main. Lock OFF vs main: verdict flat on all 25 (ro_begin_abort 1.007, rw_empty_commit 1.000, n1 1.001). Lock ON: ro_begin_abort +18.6% (+15 ns/txn), rw_empty_commit +10% (+20 ns, within noise), n1 +1.4% flat, get/* flat. Before the fix (ca27d00): off ro +4.5%, rw +9.4%; on ro +22.7%, rw +19.4%, n1 +5.4%. Instructions/op (perf stat, micro loop) main/off/on: ro 376/397/481, rw 1307/1336/1478, n1 14847/14926/15092. strace: no per-txn syscalls added by the lock file (pwrite/pread counts identical). Intermediate 5f9b238 alone left rw_empty_commit off at +6-8%: fixed by inline(never) on the lock-file arms (with_spare inlined again).

hypothesis: ADR-0023 stage 2: reaping dead readers' slots and the lock-file release order (amendment 7 adds one store to the release) leave the default path (lock file off) flat against main.
notes: Lock file OFF (default path), HEAD 164e0e9. Flat vs main on all 25 rungs per bench-ab (24 flat, 1 drift: ro_begin_abort, where LMDB drifted +8% but ZeroDB after/before is 1.000-1.013 in every round). ro_begin_abort 1.012, rw_empty_commit 1.026 (+5 ns/txn, within the 0.052 threshold), commit/batch/n1 1.015, every get/* within +-1%. Stage 1 fixed was 1.007 / 1.000 / 1.001. Amendment 7 (one more store in the lock-file release) adds nothing measurable to the default path.

hypothesis: ADR-0023 stage 2: with the lock file on, the extra store in the release order and own-PID slots keep the stage-1 single-process cost (+15 ns per read txn, +20 ns per empty write txn, n1 flat).
notes: Lock file ON, HEAD 164e0e9. get/* and commit/batch/n100 and commit/sync flat. ro_begin_abort 1.213 (+17 ns/txn; flagged unreliable by LMDB drift, ZeroDB rounds 1.198-1.232), rw_empty_commit 1.166 (+45 ns/txn, bench-ab regressed, rounds 1.113-1.239), commit/batch/n1 1.034 (+0.34 us/commit, flat, rounds 1.005-1.048). Stage 1 fixed (2b53e88) was 1.186 / 1.102 / 1.014 (+15 ns, +20 ns, +0.06 us): stage 2 raises the lock-on cost of an empty write txn by about 25 ns and of n1 by about 0.3 us. Opt-in path only.

hypothesis: ADR-0023 stage 3 Task 10: a write-txn begin that loads the map view once (base check + read view) and keeps the WRITE_MAP file-growth arm out of line removes the default-path write-begin regression added by stage 3 tasks 3-9.
notes: Lock file OFF, Graviton4 c8g.xlarge (Neoverse-V2, aarch64), 5 interleaved rounds vs main 7002d6e. Flat: 23 flat, 2 drift (ro_begin_abort, get/key/k32: LMDB drift only). rw_empty_commit 0.993 (154.4 vs 155.5 ns/txn); before the fix (f2603c3) 1.048 (+7.5 ns, regressed); stage 1 2b53e88 1.019. Micro loop (perf stat, empty write txn): 1095 -> 1028 instructions (main 1028), 428 -> 398 cycles (main 406). Not an LMDB technique: it removes a second dyn Backing::view call and an inline cold branch that the stage-3 begin had added.

hypothesis: ADR-0023 stage 3 Task 10: the same change brings the lock-file-on cost back to stage 1's on Graviton4 (write txn at or below stage 1's +30 ns vs main, read txn within noise of stage 1's +5.5 ns).
notes: Lock file ON, Graviton4, 5 interleaved rounds vs main 7002d6e, with stage 1 (2b53e88) and pre-fix HEAD (f2603c3) measured in the same rounds. rw_empty_commit: stage1 +29.8 ns (1.189), before +35.9 ns (1.228), after +27.6 ns (1.177). ro_begin_abort: stage1 +5.5 ns (1.083), before +6.5 ns (1.102), after +6.4 ns (1.097; drift-flagged, ZeroDB rounds 1.095-1.100). commit/batch/n1 1.013 flat, every get/* flat. Remaining lock-on write cost: the futex writer-word CAS and release swap (about 35 of 63 extra cycles), the T load and dyn-call plumbing; within the ADR budget (LMDB also pays a lock RMW and an unlock RMW per write txn).

hypothesis: ADR-0023 stage 3 Task 10 (review item): capture the map's page limit once at write-txn begin (from the begin's map view) instead of one Acquire load plus a dyn Backing::view call per page-extension allocation.
notes: Measured with a micro loop on Graviton4 (perf stat, instructions exact): empty write txn 1028 -> 1046 instructions, cycles 398 -> 389 off / 469 -> 471 on (noise); single-put commit 18965 -> 18991 instructions (+26). Steady-state commits draw pages from GC/loose reuse, not file extension, so the per-allocation saving never shows and the begin pays a division and a wider struct. Not a simplification either (one more field). Reverted; not benched with criterion.

hypothesis: ADR-0023 stage 3 Task 13b gate: the full ladder with the lock file on (the new default) stays within the ADR budget against main 7002d6e on Graviton4.
notes: Lock file ON (default), Graviton4 c8g.xlarge, full default-tier ladder, 3 interleaved rounds (main, HEAD on, HEAD NO_LOCK rotating). Regressed 5 of 60, flat 55, no LMDB drift. Budgeted: rw_empty_commit 1.185 (+29.8 ns/txn, Task 10 had +27.6), ro_begin_abort 1.100 (+6.8 ns/txn), env/stat/non_free 1.063 (+7 ns, shared T read). Not budgeted: env/open/reopen 20.3x (17 us -> 347 us per open; LMDB 36 us) and env/open/create 1.168 (+155 us per create): the first opener truncates the lock file to 0 and regrows it on every open (ADR-0023 amendment 10), so ext4 frees and reallocates its blocks; LMDB does not truncate. Every get/put/del/scan/seek/commit/maint rung flat.

hypothesis: ADR-0023 stage 3 Task 13b gate: the full ladder with NO_LOCK (the opt-out) is flat against main 7002d6e on Graviton4.
notes: NO_LOCK (ZERODB_BENCH_NO_LOCK=1), Graviton4 c8g.xlarge, full default-tier ladder, 3 interleaved rounds in the same runs as the lock-on line. Verdict flat: 60 flat, 0 regressed, 0 drift. rw_empty_commit and env/open/* flat.

hypothesis: ADR-0023 amendment 20: rebuilding the lock file in place instead of truncating it to zero removes the env-open cost of the lock-file default (ext4 frees and reallocates the blocks on every truncation).
notes: Graviton4 c8g.xlarge, ext4 on a gp3 root volume (not the io2 /data of the 2026-10-13 ladder), 5 interleaved rounds of env/*, lock file on. env/open/reopen 1016 -> 36.4 us per open (LMDB 37.8 us; 26.87x -> 0.96x LMDB); env/open/create 4.19 -> 3.06 ms per create (LMDB 105 us; the remaining create gap is not the lock file: with NO_LOCK it was 9.0x LMDB on 2026-10-13). env/stat and the txn rungs flat. A 3-round sample of other rungs (commit/batch/*, del/bulk/all, get/access/hot, get/val/v8*, put/api/plain) is flat: 8 of 8.

hypothesis: ADR-0024 (#73): checking a database handle's lifetime on every operation costs little on the read path once the check is a per-transaction memo of one epoch load (correctness fix, not a speedup).
notes: Accepted cost: named-database gets +2-8% (still 0.79-0.85x LMDB, which also checks the handle on every call), read-txn begin +5.8% (still 0.05x LMDB). put/api/plain, put/order/append and put/order/seq measured 6-7% faster; cause not investigated, not claimed. Mac M-series, 3 rounds.

hypothesis: #11 branch side: splitting a full branch page at its end on an end insert, as LMDB does, packs branch pages on ascending loads (fewer branch pages, shallower trees) without slowing writes.
notes: Kept for LMDB parity of tree shape (4 KiB, 20k ascending 500 B keys: 949 -> 480 branch pages, LMDB 558). Writes flat. get/access/miss -26%; get/access/hot and seq +5.5% (causes not investigated); other gets flat. Mac M-series, 3 rounds.

hypothesis: #16: branchless per-page binary search (std::hint::select_unpredictable in leaf and branch search) cuts branch mispredicts on random lookups.
notes: Gets 8-25% slower on Apple M-series (k128 +25%); not measured on Graviton, retry only with a Graviton A/B. Branch not merged.

hypothesis: #15: comparing any two keys of at most 8 bytes as zero-padded big-endian u64 (shorter first on a tie) speeds short-key and prefix compares.
notes: All get and seek rungs flat; scan/prefix/bucket 18% slower. Equal-length 4/8-byte keys already had the fast path. Branch not merged.

hypothesis: #105: a plain end insert on a full leaf moves the old last entry with the new one (LMDB parity), repacking both pages through the general split path.
notes: put/order/seq 10.5% slower (still 0.90x LMDB): every ascending split repacked the left page. Replaced by the in-place move (next entry).

hypothesis: #105: the same LMDB split point, with the old last cell removed from the left frame in place (top of the cell heap on ascending pages, so nothing else moves).
notes: All rungs flat (put/order/seq +1.8%), get/access/hot 4.5% faster. Kept for LMDB parity of leaf shape: ascending plain loads build LMDB's leaf count (more, slightly emptier leaves than before). Mac M-series, 3 rounds.

hypothesis: #45 / ADR-0026 Option B: under WRITE_MAP, C3 msyncs the used prefix [0, next_pgno) and C5 the meta page, as LMDB, instead of the whole map; fdatasync after each synchronous barrier unchanged.
notes: All flat, 16 GiB map included: the whole-map msync cost the same on 16 GiB as on 1 GiB (before side 1.605 s vs 1.607 s), so the cost #45 describes does not show on macOS at these sizes. Kept for LMDB parity of the barrier ranges. The 2x gap to LMDB is ZeroDB's second fdatasync (after C5), which LMDB does not issue. An earlier run of n1/n100 was flat with more noise (n1 0.823 +-0.258, LMDB drift 0.89). Mac M-series, 3 rounds.

hypothesis: #7: a write-cursor put of the current key applies the replace at the parked root-to-leaf path (no descent) and keeps the path when the leaf does not split, as LMDB MDB_CURRENT writes at mc_pg/mc_ki; the next step resumes instead of re-seeking.
notes: put/cursor/rewrite 0.456x (5.42x -> 2.47x LMDB), confirmed by a separate targeted 3-round run (0.456, LMDB drift 0.989). Full suite also flags read-path rungs slower (get/access/miss 1.18, get/val/* ~1.06, get/size/n1k 1.08, scan/range/* 1.42) and scan/prefix/bucket faster (0.60): the change touches only RwCursor/RwTxn write code, which these read-txn rungs never execute, so these read as code-layout shifts; needs a layout-controlled confirmation (codegen-units=1 or Linux) before merge. Pending maintainer decision. Mac M-series, 3 rounds.

hypothesis: ADR-0028: a rebalance borrow decodes the moved entry into owned buffers and rewrites the parent separator as remove + re-insert (profile: rebalance 68 % of del/bulk/half, separator rewrite alone 31 %); moving encoded cells verbatim and updating the separator in place, as LMDB's mdb_node_move / mdb_update_key, removes that work without changing tree shape.
notes: Verdict 'invalid' only because the Mac was busy (LMDB drift > 3 % on 5 rungs); every round of every rebalance rung improved: after/before 0.44-0.64 bulk/all, 0.44-0.53 bulk/half, 0.38-0.58 cursor/drain, 0.64-0.83 churn, 0.36-0.41 range/half; untouched clear/all 0.87-1.13. Golden logical images unchanged. crud-bench (500k, 1.5 KB values, 16 KiB, one delete per txn, 48 threads) deletes only +7-39 % per round: that phase is commit-bound, ~78 % of commit in MetaPage::encode_with_annex (meta free-list annex re-encoded per commit). Report: benches/results/2026-10-18-delete-rebalance-node-move-mac.md.

hypothesis: Iterator::nth (what skip calls) crosses whole leaves by entry count instead of stepping, bound-testing and resolving each skipped entry; LMDB's C cursor can only step one entry at a time.
notes: scan/skip_take fwd/rev 15x faster than before, about 11x faster than LMDB (skip 5000, take 100, 50k keys, 256 B values). Same session, full scan suite: range/prefix/edge/meta flat. scan/full fwd/rev read 1.17-1.24x slower in every run (recorded here as unreliable: LMDB drifted 6% and 4% in this verdict's run; a run with drift under 2% called them regressed at 1.21x and 1.24x), but the plain-scan source is unchanged (ascend_* identical to main; RoRange::in_bounds kept single-caller via a const generic so LLVM still inlines it, key compare included, into next), and a control build adding only the never-instantiated cursor skip code showed the same +13% median while an A/A with byte-identical binaries showed 0.95x: read as code-layout sensitivity of this rung on M-series, to confirm on Graviton. An earlier version split the bound test into a free function: LLVM then outlined it from RoRange::next and scan/full was 1.4x slower. Mac M-series, 3 rounds.

hypothesis: Graviton4 confirmation of the leaf-skipping Iterator::nth (same change as the 2026-10-19 Mac entry): does scan/full stay flat on the primary target?
notes: Graviton4 c8g.xlarge, Ubuntu 24.04, 4 KiB pages, 3 interleaved rounds, base 8252ae5. scan/full fwd/rev flat at 1.000x with LMDB drift under 0.3%, so the 1.2x read on the Mac was code layout, not the change. scan/range flat. scan/skip_take fwd/rev 4.3x faster than before and about 2x faster than LMDB: a smaller gain than on the Mac's 16 KiB pages because a 4 KiB leaf holds fewer entries to cross at once.

hypothesis: #42: reserve disk blocks 64 MiB ahead of the commit write high-water mark (macOS F_PREALLOCATE, Linux fallocate KEEP_SIZE; best-effort) so file-extending commits stop growing the file one write at a time. LMDB does not preallocate (default mode grows by pwrite; WRITEMAP ftruncates to the map size, sparse).
notes: Mac shared with other jobs (load 8-14 on 8 CPUs), three bench-ab runs. Targeted rung after/before: 0.717 (3 rounds, LMDB drift 0.80), 0.990 +-0.32 (5 rounds, LMDB drift 1.002, the only clean row), 0.896 +-0.73 (7 rounds, drift 0.85): no resolvable win. Standalone C micro (pwritev appends, 3 rounds): no-sync 1 page/commit 7.7-8.3 -> 5.6-6.0 us/commit; plain fsync 64 pages/commit 187-373 -> 128-174 us; F_FULLFSYNC commits (what ZeroDB issues on macOS) 8.3-11.3 ms either way, within noise. APFS keeps the reserved blocks after close (st_blocks 64 MiB over st_size), a disk-usage difference from LMDB. Needs a Linux/Graviton A/B of a durable growth-heavy load before an opt-in option is designed.

hypothesis: Issue #8: a one-key no-sync commit spends ZeroDB-only CPU on the meta page encode (byte-wise CRC32C over ~200 bytes, a fresh page allocation zeroed twice); slicing-by-8 CRC tables and an env-held all-zero meta buffer (only the encoded prefix rewritten and re-cleared) remove it without changing the bytes written.
notes: Mac M-series, loaded host (load 3-70 during the session). Wall time is syscall-bound on macOS: full suite 3 rounds commit/batch/n1 0.968 (+-0.180, LMDB drift 1.010), targeted 5 rounds 0.953 (+-0.083, drift 1.041); nothing regressed beyond drift. getrusage user CPU per one-key commit (scratch harness, NO_LOCK both engines, 8-10 interleaved rounds): LMDB 1.50 us, before 4.17 us, after 3.45 us (-17%); kernel time unchanged. Empty write txn user CPU 114 -> 113 ns (LMDB 25 ns): untouched, since an empty commit writes no meta. A first version kept the buffer in the writer guard and cost empty txns +4 ns (bigger RwTxn to move); moved to an env-level mutex taken only by meta-writing commits. Empty-txn profile (NO_LOCK): ~37% memmove of the 888-byte RwTxn across write_txn/commit, ~13% three uncontended mutex pairs (writer flag x2, snapshot cell), drop glue; boxing the txn in heed-zerodb measured +22 ns (malloc > moves), #[inline] wrappers -2% (noise). With the default lock file on macOS both engines are syscall-bound (fcntl vs SysV semop).
